svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.23.16.5 Lumber Roof Sheathing
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Lumber Roof Sheathing

g.text: 286 mm or less wide, all ends supported,
Installed diagonally in the limits of (2)
WHICH SENTENCE APPLIES, SMAX AND HWP LIMITS
or less wide, ends supported, joints
kPa or more but under 1.2 kPa, (2)
over 0.8, or HWP 1.2 kPa or more,

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Lumber roof sheathing is not more than 286 mm
(11¼″) wide and is applied so that all ends
are supported with end joints staggered.
Lumber roof sheathing is installed diagonally,
where
(a) the seismic design parameter, Smax, Site
Class C is greater than 0.47 but not greater than
0.8, or (b) the 1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure
(HWP) is equal to or greater than 0.80 kPa but
less than 1.2 kPa.
Lumber roof sheathing is designed according to
Part 4, where
(a) the seismic design parameter, Smax, for Site
Class C is greater than 0.8, or (b) he
1-in-50-year hourly wind pressure (HWP) is equal
to or greater than 1.2 kPa.
As printed: "he 1-in-50-year" in (3)(b). Chart shows the Smax and HWP limits only. Board sizes are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.16.5. (page 9-225)
